answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the harbor index resolves every citation against the juniper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the trellis audit keeps the resolved set. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 6 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
